headlines.article_text: Comcast (CMCSA) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Comcast topped analyst earnings expectations for the third quarter. Streaming service Peacock hit profitability for the second consecutive quarter. Comcast is in the process of spinning off its media business into a separate publicly traded company. Theme parks and the connectivity business continued to face pressure. In this article CMCSA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 2:54 02:54 Comcast beats on top and bottom lines in Q3 Squawk Box Comcast beat Wall Street's expectations for third-quarter earnings — despite headwinds in its theme parks business — thanks to continued strength in its media unit. The company's Peacock streaming service reported a quarterly profit for the second time since its launch in 2020, posting $261 million in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization on $1.8 billion in revenue. Peacock maintained 48 million paid subscribers, flat from last quarter and up 17% year over year. Comcast said the streamer demonstrated strong retention despite raising subscription prices in August. The platform continued to reap the benefits of record-high viewership for the FIFA World Cup, as the final games played out at the beginning of the quarter and aired on NBCUniversal's Telemundo and on Peacock. Revenue in Comcast's media division, which includes the streaming service, rose 13% compared with the third quarter last year to $5.4 billion. The overall content and experiences unit, which also includes its film studio and theme parks, saw revenue rise 6.5%. Comcast's connectivity and platforms sector, however, continued to face pressure, with revenue down 2.7% year over year. The company reported a net loss in domestic broadband residential customers of 144,000 and a net loss in its cable customers of 274,000 during the period. Its mobile business added 368,000 customers. After years of stagnating growth in broadband and heightened competition from wireless providers like Verizon and T-Mobile, Comcast announced in January 2025 that it would refocus on its mobile business and pursue more competitive pricing plans. "We feel mobile remains a tremendous growth opportunity for us. It's a capital light model, [which] leverages our existing customer broadband base," Steve Croney, CEO of Comcast's connectivity and platforms division, said on an earnings call on Thursday. Shares of Comcast rose roughly 5% following the report. Here's how Comcast performed for the period ended Sept. 30 compared with what analysts expected, according to LSEG: Earnings per share: $1.07 adjusted vs. 98 cents expected Revenue: $29.3 billion vs. $29.28 billion expected In June, Comcast announced plans to spin off NBCUniversal and European media business Sky from its core cable, wireless and business services units. The split, which Comcast said would take about a year, will create two separate publicly traded companies. Comcast co-CEO Mike Cavanagh said on the earnings call that the company is "on track" to complete the transaction by mid-2027. "While there is still significant work ahead, we have a clear path to completion and remain focused on creating two companies with the strategic flexibility, financial strength, and leadership to compete and grow independently," Cavanagh said. "We have tremendous confidence in the future of both companies." The split comes after Comcast spun off most of its cable networks , along with an array of digital businesses, into Versant . That separation was completed in January. For the third quarter, Comcast's revenue was 6% lower than the year-ago period. However, adjusting for the impact of the Versant spin, revenue was essentially flat year over year, Comcast said. Net income for the period was $3.45 billion, or 97 cents per share, compared with $3.33 billion, or 90 cents per share, in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusting for one-time items, including investments and the value of certain intangible assets, Comcast reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.07. The company's theme park revenue fell 4.4% during the period to $2.6 billion, which the company attributed to "cyclical headwinds" and lower revenue from admissions, dented by promotional activity. Adjusted EBITDA for the division sank 17%. The weakness in theme parks comes despite continued investment in the sector with the opening of a new coaster at Universal Studios Hollywood this quarter and Universal's largest theme park property, Epic Universe, last year. Theme park rival Disney reported record quarterly revenue in its park division in August. Cavanagh said on the earnings call that in addition to macroeconomic factors, Universal's theme parks struggled due to superior marketing from competitors and technological challenges at Epic Universe. Cavanagh cited new hires, including that of Luc Bondar to the role of chief brand and commercial officer for Universal Destinations and Experiences, as steps the company was taking to address these challenges. "Looking ahead, we expect performance to strengthen as we move through 2027, with a return to growth in the second half of the year," Cavanagh said. "We remain confident in the underlying strength of the business." Comcast's studios division reported revenue of $2.97 billion, down 1.1% from the third quarter last year. Adjusted EBITDA for the segment, however, increased 18.6% to $402 million, thanks to lower operating expenses. The July theatrical release of "The Odyssey," which became Universal's highest-grossing film of all time, boosted the division. Meanwhile, content licensing revenue was down 23.7% from the comparable quarter, leading to the decrease in studio revenue, according to Comcast. headlines.article_text: Procter & Gamble (PG) Q1 2027 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Procter & Gamble topped Wall Street's estimates for its quarterly earnings and revenue. The company updated its full-year sales forecast to reflect its acquisition of Thorne. CFO Andre Schulten said the company continues to see a bifurcated economy. In this article PG Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 7:50 07:50 P&G CFO Andre Schulten on Q1 results: Driven by 4% organic sales growth Squawk Box Procter & Gamble on Thursday reported quarterly earnings and revenue that beat analysts' expectations, fueled by growing demand for its laundry detergent and home care products. Shares of the company rose more than 5% in morning trading. Here's what the company reported for the three-month period ended Sept. 30 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $2.00 adjusted vs. $1.88 expected Revenue: $23.3 billion vs. $22.8 billion expected P&G reported fiscal first-quarter net income attributable to the company of $4.73 billion, or $1.97 per share, down from $4.75 billion, or $1.95 per share, a year earlier. Excluding restructuring costs and other items, the company earned $2 per share. Net sales rose 4% to $23.3 billion. Bottles of Dawn dish spray are displayed for sale at a Target store on August 4, 2026 in Washington, DC. Kevin Carter | Getty Images P&G reported volume growth of 2.4%, a strong start for its new fiscal year. Like many consumer companies, P&G has seen demand for its products weaken as shoppers have become more value-conscious. Executives have previously said that consumers are now using every last drop of shampoo or laundry detergent, and value packs have become more popular. In fiscal 2026, P&G reported just one quarter of volume growth. P&G is still seeing signs of a bifurcated economy, CFO Andre Schulten said on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Thursday. High-income consumers are willing to trade up to new products, even a $30 shampoo, while low-income consumers are trying to make brands like Tide and Pampers work for their tight budgets. The company has tried to address both ends of the spectrum with promotional pricing, new pack sizes and product innovation that can command higher prices. New premium products like Pampers Amore and Pantene's Abundant & Strong haircare line have helped P&G grow market share in those categories, executives said. Adding to P&G's challenges, the competitive environment is "intense," Schulten said on the company's quarterly earnings call. "We are getting the balance between pricing and product improvements, package improvements, claims, communication and retail execution right," Schulten told analysts. "But it's also a very fragile balance that we want to make sure we we don't compromise on, so we will price, and we will price with innovation, not jeopardizing the top-line momentum." P&G's top-performing division was fabric and home care, which includes brands like Tide and Febreze. The segment's volume rose 4.3% in the quarter, helped by stronger demand for laundry detergent and fabric enhancers. The company's baby, feminine and family care segment and its beauty business both reported volume growth of more than 2%. P&G's grooming division saw volume shrink 0.4% in the quarter. The segment includes Gillette and Venus razors. The company's healthcare business was the laggard of the portfolio this quarter. Its volume fell 2.9% as demand for oral healthcare products, like Crest toothpaste, and personal healthcare items, like Pepto-Bismol, shrank. The company is expecting continued "geopolitical and economic challenges," but P&G is on track to meet its guidance, CEO Shailesh Jejurikar said in a statement. For fiscal 2027, P&G reiterated its forecast for core earnings per share in a range of $6.89 to $7.11. The company is now projecting all-in sales growth in the range of 2% to 4% compared with the prior year, up from its previous outlook of 1% to 3%. The change reflects its acquisition of supplements brand Thorne , which closed Oct. 1. headlines.title: Blackstone's Jon Gray says CoreWeave can 'find a way through' financing pressure
headlines.summary: Blackstone COO Jon Gray says CoreWeave's underlying business is strong despite concerns over its mounting debt.
headlines.article_text: Blackstone's Jon Gray on CoreWeave financing pressure Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points CoreWeave is facing challenges over the financing for their AI buildouts, but has a strong CEO, said Blackstone's Jon Gray. The company will "find a way through it," he said. Gray also said Blackstone delivered for its clients in the third quarter, and expects a robust fourth quarter ahead. In this article BX CRWV Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT VIDEO 8:23 08:23 Watch CNBC's full interview with Blackstone President and COO Jon Gray CoreWeave has been battered over concerns about its massive debt, but Blackstone chief operating officer Jon Gray believes the so-called neocloud company will weather the storm. Right now, CoreWeave and its neocloud peers are facing challenges over the capital needed to deliver on their promises, he said in an interview with CNBC's " Squawk Box " Thursday. "Some of these companies have very talented CEOs. CoreWeave is a good example of this," Gray said. "They'll find a way through it, but that's the challenge they face. The underlying business is actually quite strong." CoreWeave has seen its stock sink , bond yields rise and spreads on its credit default swaps widen over the past week as investors became nervous about how the company will continue to finance its data centers, and at what cost. The company has roughly $51.6 billion in total debt, including about $35 billion in notes, bonds and loans. Coreweave's one-month performance Demand for computing power, however, is strong, said Gray. He is seeing that across the board in the private companies the firm holds. At the same time, there is a constraint in delivering supply, he said. "For the neo clouds, if they can get to the other side, the pricing of compute is up 50%," he said. "Their legacy chips are worth much more than people thought. Their data centers are leased below market." Shares of CoreWeave sank 3.55% on Thursday, and are down 14% over the past week. Blackstone earnings Gray spoke with CNBC after Blackstone reported its third-quarter results, which came in mixed. Its stock was up 4% on Thursday. Blackstone saw quarterly revenue of $3.22 billion, short of the $3.28 billion expected from analysts polled by LSEG. Its adjusted earnings of $1.32 per share, however, topped the $1.26 consensus estimate. It was a "challenging quarter with markets" thanks to high energy prices and the rise in Treasury yields, Gray said. However, the firm delivered for its clients, he noted. "Across the board, our flagship strategies beat comparable public market indices and that's what we care most about," he said. Blackstone year to date He anticipates a strong fourth quarter and 2027, despite some cross-currents like the rising cost of capital, government deficits and some crowding out of capital due to the AI infrastructure build. However, good news is there is underlying economic and earnings strength, he said. Gray also expects initial public offerings to resume once the market and geopolitical situation calms a bit. He said investors just need to have some patience. "We have a long-term approach, and we feel very good about where we position capital for our investors, the growth of those companies, the growth of those assets, and that's what gives us confidence," he said. "At some point, the wider window will open, and when that happens, we and others will sell even more." A critical flaw in the programming language PHP was revealed "earlier than it was supposed to have been", which mean hackers started checking websites to see if they could exploit the vulnerability, an expert has said. Yui Mok | Pa Images | Getty Images The tech world is racing to implement fixes after the discovery of critical security vulnerabilities in software used to power much of the internet. The software, known as PHP, is an open-source programming language widely used to power websites and web applications. The discovery of the flaws prompted urgent warnings from governments worldwide, while tech giants including Google, OpenAI and Amazon have been involved in efforts to uncover the vulnerabilities, detect potential attacks and protect affected systems. The two vulnerabilities, collectively known as "PHP2Shell," could allow hackers to remotely execute malicious code on affected servers, potentially exposing sensitive data, according to cybersecurity researchers. While not every website using PHP is necessarily vulnerable, the software's widespread use has raised concerns about the potential scale of attacks. The U.S. National Security Agency on Wednesday urged organizations using PHP to prepare security updates addressing the vulnerabilities, warning that the flaws could provide attackers with direct access to server file systems and databases. The agency recommended taking affected systems offline until the vulnerabilities are fully addressed if immediate updates are not possible. The Federal Bureau of Investigation also warned that malicious actors could exploit the vulnerabilities to execute code remotely, putting sensitive data and networks at risk. Amazon said its threat intelligence team had detected attempts to exploit the vulnerabilities before they were publicly disclosed, using its MadPot threat detection system, which monitors suspicious activity across internet-facing infrastructure. It said the findings suggest malicious actors were already attempting to exploit the vulnerabilities. However, Amazon said it remains unclear how the attackers obtained information about the flaws ahead of their disclosure. Meanwhile, Google and OpenAI highlighted the growing role of artificial intelligence in identifying and addressing cybersecurity threats. Google said its cybersecurity unit Wiz used AI models to help find and investigate the vulnerabilities, while its Gemini AI contributed to efforts to assess the flaws, test potential attacks and verify security patches. OpenAI said researchers working with its AI models had also helped uncover critical vulnerabilities in PHP. The company said it had spent the past two months leading a coalition of software maintainers, cybersecurity researchers and security providers to coordinate fixes and prepare protective measures ahead of public disclosure. The ChatGPT maker described the flaws as among the most significant security issues in recent memory, highlighting both the potential of advanced AI systems to identify vulnerabilities in widely used software and the risk that similar capabilities could be exploited by cybercriminals. Cloudflare, which provides cybersecurity and website infrastructure services, said it had deployed protections against the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities through its web application firewall. The company said its measures were designed to help block malicious requests targeting affected systems, providing an additional layer of defense as organizations work to install software updates. The PHP development team has released security fixes, with authorities urging website operators to identify affected versions and apply the updates as quickly as possible. The carrier expects to earn between $2.60 and $2.85 a share on an adjusted basis this year, down from its forecast in July of between $3.25 to as much as $4.25 a share. It said it expects to grow capacity by up to 4% year over year. "Demand remained strong as we lapped last year's bag fee and other commercial initiatives, reinforcing our belief that the earnings power we've built is durable, even with significantly higher fuel costs," Jordan said in an earnings release. The airline said its average passenger fare was $231.69 in the third quarter, up almost 27% from the same quarter of 2025. A spokesman said that number does not include add-on fees. The number of revenue passengers carried fell 3.2% to 33.47 million people. But Jordan told CNBC's Phil LeBeau that demand was strong across every geography and product. "The consumer is incredibly strong and we do not see that abating," Jordan said. "We're seeing strength in both the holiday period and the non-holiday period." Under pressure to grow revenue, Southwest has been remaking its longtime business model over the past several years, scrapping its old policies like two free checked bags per passenger and open seating. In its place, Southwest has started charging for many seat assignments and added a bag fee, similar to major competitors. For the third quarter, Southwest posted net income of $270 million, or 55 cents a share, up from $54 million or 10 cents a share a year earlier. Revenue rose more than 21% to $8.42 billion. Adjusting for one-time items, Southwest reported 66 cents a share.
